headline: Adopted decision for 11 Kingston Road second-story addition; granted Donald Alexis an extension for his 89 Vernon Street home project, 4-1.
summary: The board heard a request for a side-yard setback variance to build a second floor over the existing single-story home at 11 Kingston Road. Neighbors asked about the side of the house, the back yard, and the fence and walls. The board adopted its Findings of Fact and Proposed Decision for that case, and granted an extension to petitioner Donald Alexis by a 4-1 vote.
decisions: Adopted the Proposed Findings of Fact for Case No. 2026-18, 5-0 roll call.
Adopted the Proposed Decision for Case No. 2026-18, 5-0 roll call.
Granted an extension to petitioner Donald Alexis, 4-1 vote; Mr. Sergi voted no.

plain_text:
City of Waltham 
Zoning Board of Appeals 
July 14, 2026 
The Zoning Board of Appeals held a public hearing at 7:00 P.M. on Tuesday, July 
14, 2026 in the Public Meeting Room of the Arthur Clark Government Center, 119 School 
Street, Waltham, MA. 
In attendance were John Sergi, Chair, and members Mark Hickernell, Joseph 
Attardo, Glenna Gelineau and Matthew Deveaux. 
Mr. Sergi: Tonight we have a new case and an extension. 
The first order ofbnsiness tonight is to approve the minutes of June 23, 2026. May I 
have a motion to approve the minutes of June 23, 2026, please? 
On motion of Mr. Hickernell, seconded by Ms. Gelineau, the board voted to approve 
the Minutes of June 23, 2026. 
Mr. Sergi: So we have approved the minutes of June 23, 2026. 
Okay, the first case we are going to hear tonight is a new case, Case No. 2026-18, 
Petitioner/Owner Scott Douglas and Callaghan McCarthy. If the clerk would be kind 
enough to read the petition, please? 
The clerk then read the Petition in Case No. 2026-18, Petitioner/Owner: Scott 
Douglas and Callaghan McCarthy. Nature Of Appeal/Petition: Variance. Subject Matter: 
1
To allow for the construction of a second floor over the existing single-story. Location And 
Zoning District: 11 Kingston Road; Residence A-3 Zoning District. Provisions Of Zoning 
Ordinance Involved: § 4.11 - Side-yard Setbacks. Specific Relief Sought: Petitioners 
require relief for construction of a second story over the existing single-story ranch home 
that will sit 14.82 feet from the northern side-yard lot line and 14.57 feet from the southern 
side-yard lot line where 15 feet is required. 
Mr. Sergi: May we hear from the Petitioner or the Petitioner's representative, 
please. 
Attorney Bret Francis, Law Office at 10 Hammer Street, Waltham came forward 
and presented each member with a copy of his brief. 
Attorney Francis then read his brief into the record and submitted photos of the 
proposed addition. 
Mr. Sergi: What about on the side of the house? 
Mr. Francis: I don't have a rendering for the side of the house but it's only going 
straight up. It won't be coming out at all. 
Mr. Keiejo: It's a pretty house but it's the side of the house that's important. 
Mr. Sergi: So it looks like this is going to fit in the neighborhood because I know 
that the house next door is two stories, right, and the house on the other side is two stories. 
So this is just something that's similar to what's there in the neighborhood. 
2
Mr. Francis: That's correct. 
Mr. Sergi: And it looks like you 're using the typical siding and all that. 
Mr. Francis: Pretty traditional. 
Mr. Sergi: I'll open it up to the board. Joe, do you have any questions? 
Mr. Attardo: No questions. 
Mr. Sergi: Glenna? 
Ms. Gelineau: No. 
Mr. Sergi: Matt? 
Mr. Deveaux: No. 
Mr. Sergi: Mark? 
Mr. Hickernell: No. 
Mr. Sergi: I don't have any questions. All right, I'll open it up to the audience. 
Is there anyone in the audience that's against the petition as presented tonight that would 
like to come up and speak? 
3
Seeing none. Is there anyone seeking information? 
Michael Kiejzo, 17 Kingston Road, Waltham, north side? So my question is, what is 
the house going to look like on the side of the house because it's kind of high. 
Mr. Kiejzo to Mr. McCarthy: So what would your house look like when you build it 
on that side of the house? 
Callaghan McCarthy, the developer, showed some pictures from his cell phone to 
Mr. Kiejzo and Jennifer Imbaro. 
Mr. Sergi: Cal, I think whatever you are showing them you should show the board. 
Mr. Douglas: Can I jump in? 
Scott Douglas, 61 Arcadia Ave, Waltham: So I just wanted to show you that the 
house ins't moving at all. The house isn't. The foundation isn't, the side of the house is 
going straight up the entire length. 
Mr. McCarthy: Literally what we are trying to do is go straight up. 
Mr. Kiejzo: Oh, okay, I get it. I have a whole bunch of other questions. I know the 
back yard, the lady that was there before, she wasn't really all there, and she put up cinder 
blocks all over the place. Are you guys going to remove those? 
Mr. McCarthy: So we are going to do what's best for the market. We want it to 
4
look good for a buyer. So you can imagine we are going to make it look nice. 
Mr. Kiejzo: I just recently the other day finally cut down the weeds in the back 
yard, the seven foot tall weeds. Are you going to maintain the up-keep on that on a regular 
basis or just once every six months like before? 
Mr. McCarthy: We will be doing that on a regular basis. 
Mr. Kiejzo: Awesome. Thank you. 
Mr. Sergi: You can talk to him separately. I think he's satisfied. 
Do you want to show the board those pictures? 
Mr. Francis: And I can submit them to you via email if you like. 
Mr. Sergi: We'll just take a glance at them. So I got an idea of what they are. 
(Mr. McCarthy showed the board renderings of the photos that were on his cell 
phone.) 
Mr. Sergi: While they are doing that we have a correspondence from a Jennifer 
Umbaro. Jennifer, would you like to read this into the record? 
Jennifer Umbaro, 5 Kingston Road, Waltham came forward and read her email 
5
dated July 8, 2026 addressed to the board into the record. 
Mr. Sergi: Do you want to address some of this. I think yon already addressed some 
ofit. 
Mr. McCarthy: So maintenance wise, now we have somebody on the hook. We have 
been blown off by six different landscapers, so now we have somebody on the hook who is 
doing the landscaping every week. The fence and wall, I can picture the fence, it's the thin 
black not wrought iron but trying to look like a wrought iron fence. That would all be 
replaced. I can't really picture the stacking block wall with the - - - (there was a side 
discussion with the two neighbors). 
I have a feeling it's not good for a buyer and we are going to replace it. One thing I 
would say is, so, we did a property. We actually kind of sort of did this exact thing on 59 
Maravista Ave. at the top of the hill by Lakeview and my masons are phenomenal. I don't 
even use stacking block. Everything is real stone and the fence work I do myself and we do 
nice fence work. I can't exactly tell you what we are going to do for a stacking block or 
whatever other than we do nice work and we want it to sell it on the market. So I don't 
know exactly what. 
Ms. lmbaro: The concern is maintaining the fence. 
Mr. McCarthy: Sure. 
Ms. lmbaro: I believe the fence belongs to your house. 
Mr. McCarthy: Sure. So what we would probably end up doing is replacing the 
6
fence entirely and replace it with a white vinyl picket fence. I have a bnnch of examples in 
Waltham that I can show you. We probably will do a four foot fence unless and maybe in 
the back you would want a six foot. We don't really care. Front yards I think four feet 
looks like a lot better than six. It kind of looks like two neighbors hate each other when it's 
a six foot fence in the front yard. So we would probably do a traditional picket fence in the 
front yard. I have plenty of examples. And I can't picture grade change but if there was a 
retaining wall to be had, it would be in real stone. Our masons are doing exactly this right 
now on Greer Street one street down from the Northeast School. 
(Mr. McCarthy went over photos of stone walls with the neighbors.) 
Mr. Francis: We will definitely switch contact information and I would also remind 
you that the building department is very responsive. If you feel it's not being built 
accordingly, or have any complaint whatsoever, please, the Waltham Building Department 
is very responsive to abutters. 
Mr. Sergi: Is there anyone in the audience in favor of the petition as presented? 
Tuo people raised their hand in favor. 
Mr. Sergi: If there is no other further questions from the board, I'll proceed with 
the Findings of Fact and the Proposed Decision. So, the Finding of Facts, Counselor, and 
the Proposed Decision, have they been changed since you filed them? 
Mr. Francis: No changes. 
Mr. Sergi: So, I'd ask for a motion to waive the reading of the Proposed Findings of 
7
Fact and the Proposed Decision since they have been on file and we've already read them. 
On motion of Mr. Hickernell, seconded by Ms. Gelineau, the board voted to waive 
the reading of the Proposed Findings of Fact and the Proposed Decision as they have been 
filed and available for public inspection. 
Mr. Sergi: So we have waived the reading of the Proposed Findings of Fact and the 
Proposed Decision since they have been on file and we have read them. So, with that done, 
may I have a motion on the Proposed Findings of Fact as presented tonight. 
On motion of Mr. Hickernell, seconded by Ms. Gelineau, the board voted that the 
Proposed Findings of Fact be adopted by the board as the board's Findings of Fact. 
Roll call: Mr. Attardo, yes; Ms. Gelineau, yes; Mr. Deveaux, yes; Mr. Hickernell, yes 
and Mr Sergi, yes. 
Mr. Sergi: On the Proposed Decision as presented. 
On motion of Mr. Hickernell, seconded by Ms. Gelineau, the board voted that the 
Proposed Decision be adopted by the board as the board's Decision. 
Roll call: Mr. Attardo, yes; Ms. Gelineau, yes; Mr. Deveaux, yes; Mr. Hickernell, yes 
and Mr Sergi, yes. 
Mr. Sergi: Good luck! 
Mr. Sergi: Okay, we have one more matter to discuss tonight. It's an extension 
8
request by Donald Alexis. Would you like to come to the podium, sir? 
Donald Alexis, 89 Vernon Street, Waltham came forward. 
Mr. Sergi: My understanding in reading this, Mr. Alexis, is you're asking for 
another extension. 
Mr. Alexis: Yes. So technically the house is done. So, but the contractor there was 
infiltration in the basement, we have to go back and get it re-fixed and inspected so that's 
why I need to get an extension. I went to the engineering department so I'm expecting 
some work I think to happen there but the house is completely done. 
Mr. Sergi: I just want to understand, is this the fifth extension request, Matt? 
Mr. Deveaux: This will be the sixth extension request. It started in 2022. 
Mr. Sergi: Why should the board entertain this? I mean, we've given you five 
extensions. 
Mr. Alexis: I started the job and it isn't whole house like 1896, the foundation and 
then the foundation caved in as we tried to connect the whole house. I ran out of money 
and I tried to do it and I didn't want to take a new loan to do it. We have been under nickel 
and dime to get it done. 
Mr. Sergi: You keep coming back and asking for extensions. Each time you come 
9
back you say you're going to finish it and end up here again. 
I don't know, I would just like to hear from the rest of the board. How do you feel 
Joe on this? 
Mr. Attardo: Ifwe put something here this will be the last. 
Mr. Sergi: We already did that Joe. 
Mr. Gelineau: Is there a reason we can't extend it? 
Mr. Sergi: I just think it's just- - -
Ms. Gelineau: What happens ifwe don't extend it? 
Mr. Sergi: What happens if he just keeps asking for extensions? 
Ms. Gelineau: What happens ifwe don't extend it. What happens to him? 
Mr, Deveaux: Well, he's also out of compliance with the building department. 
Mr. Sergi: He's going to have to reapply probably for whatever approvals he needs 
to continue it, Glenna. I don't lmow the specifics. But all I know is that he's been here five 
times and he keeps extending it and I think the board's been very gracious in granting 
extension after extension. I'm not inclined to give an extension tonight. That's my opinion. 
Ms. Gelineau: It's okay with me. I don't think it's anything that he's done 
10
intentionally. To give him one more chance, I don't think is - - -
Mr. Sergi: That's what we said last time. 
Ms. Gelineau: I know but he just a homeowner. He's not a contractor, he's not 
doing anything. 
Mr. Deveaux: I know if it's out of compliance with the building department, is there 
another reason why he keeps asking for the extensions. 
Ms. Gelineau: I can't answer that. 
Mr. Deveaux: I mean that's why - - - He's like, hey, he had X amount of time to get 
the job done. He's not getting the job done. 
Ms. Gelineau: Based on his permit. 
Mr. Deveaux: Based on his permit. His permit has expired. 
Ms. Gelineau: Okay. So by us extending does that automatically extend his permit 
or does he have go go back and get a new permit. 
Mr. Sergi: He's got to do an as-built survey. He's got to do another final re­
inspection. 
Ms. Gelineau: Either way? 
Mr. Sergi: Ya. Right. It says in his letter. 
11
Mr. Deveaux: He can't go and do those things unless he's extending. 
Ms. Gelineau: And then what happens to him? 
Mr.Sergi: He can reapply. 
Mr. Deveaux: If they accept those things, yes, this will be all done. If they don't 
accept them then he's going to need yet another extension and yet another extension. I'm 
just more or less, I've done plenty of things in the city myself too and I didn't take this long 
to get it done. Well, I'm not saying I won't grant it, it's just you've got to get it done, you 
can't not get done. You said the last time this was the last time. So, is this the last, last 
time? I don't know. 
Mr. Alexis: So I've done all the final approvals. So when I went to engineering, so 
that construction contractor is not from Waltham so we had to call to an excavation to get 
it inspected and that didn't happen, now we have to go back and fix it. We have to pass all 
inspections and go back to the building department to get the final inspection. 
Mr. Sergi: Mark, do you have any questions or comments? 
Mr. Hickernell: Mr. Sergi: Who is this house being built for. Is this for the CICD 
or-•! 
Mr. Alexis: No, no. This is my home, My family has been in Waltham since 69. I 
played basketball for High School, I bought it from Brasco in 2013 so now we have an 
extended family. 
Mr Hickernell: So CICD is just for identification purposes. 
12
Mr. Alexis: That's my email address. 
Mr. Hickernell: It probably has nothing to do with the project. That's the only 
question that I have. 
Mr. Sergi: With that said, may I have a motion on the request? 
On motion of Ms. Gelineau, seconded by Mr. Hickernell, the board voted to grant 
the extension to the petitioner. 
Roll call: Mr. Attardo, yes; Ms. Gelineau, yes; Mr. Deveaux, yes; Mr. Hickernell, yes 
and Mr. Sergi, no. 
The vote was 4-1 in favor. 
Mr. Sergi: It's been granted. 
Mr. Alexis: Thank you very much. 
Mr. Sergi: One more motion is in order. 
On motion of Mr. Hickernell, seconded by Mr. Attardo, the board voted to adjourn 
at 7:29 P.M.
